sections.label: Vaccination rate and fiscal spending
sections.summary: Singapore's vaccination rate is among the world's highest, and it budgeted around $100 billion, eventually spending $72.3 billion over eight Budgets in FY2020 and FY2021.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Our vaccination rate is among the highest in the world.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We budgeted around $100 billion to respond to this crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We eventually spent $72.3 billion, rolled out over eight Budgets in FY2020 and FY2021.

sections.label: Past Reserves drawn for fiscal response
sections.summary: The FY2020 and FY2021 fiscal response included $36.9 billion drawn from past Reserves with the President's concurrence.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Our fiscal response for the two years – FY2020 and FY2021 – included $36.9 billion drawn from our past Reserves, with the President's concurrence and I thank the President for giving her assent to the use of the past Reserves.

sections.label: Pew survey on national unity
sections.summary: A Pew Research Centre global survey found Singapore is one of few countries where the sense of unity is higher today than before the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: According to a global survey done by Pew Research Centre, we are one of the few countries in the world where the sense of unity is higher today than before the pandemic.

sections.label: Migrant worker dormitory outbreak
sections.summary: Infection protocols in migrant worker dormitories were insufficient, causing a major outbreak that Government, private firms and NGOs brought under control.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For instance, our infection protocols in the migrant worker dormitories were insufficient and we faced a major outbreak which almost resulted in a disaster.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It took a herculean effort by the Government, private firms and NGOs to bring the situation under control, and to provide migrant workers with the care and support they needed.

sections.label: Hindsight on mask-wearing position
sections.summary: On hindsight, Singapore should have been less definitive on mask-wearing from the outset and encouraged facial coverings while ramping up surgical mask production.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: On hindsight, we should have been less definitive in our position on mask-wearing from the outset.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We should have encouraged facial coverings of some sort, including homemade masks, while we ramped up the production of surgical masks.

sections.label: Simplified health protocols and SMMs
sections.summary: Singapore learned along the way and eventually simplified the rules to just three health protocols and five SMMs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Fortunately, we did learn along the way and eventually, simplified the rules to just three health protocols and five SMMs.

sections.label: Earlier border tightening reflection
sections.summary: The speaker says a margin of safety and more aggressive border measures should have been built in earlier as the virus spread.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Reflecting on our experience, our sense is that, at the beginning, we should have built in a margin of safety and tightened border measures more aggressively the moment the virus showed signs of spreading across borders, even though there might have been some risk of us overreacting to these signals.

sections.label: LTP Holders entry timing
sections.summary: The speaker says LTP Holders could have been let back in sooner, or some groups prioritised, such as those with families here.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: On reflection, we could have let the LTP Holders back in sooner, or at least prioritised entry for some groups, such as those with families here.

sections.label: Few China arrivals, no tightening
sections.summary: Few arrivals came from China and few had COVID-19, so restrictions were not tightened then.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Furthermore, our arrivals from China were relatively few, and only a small proportion of them had COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We were therefore confident that the Chinese arrivals would not put too much pressure on our healthcare system and we decided at that time not to tighten restrictions.

sections.label: Dedicated public health centre
sections.summary: A dedicated centre for public health will be set up, similar to Centres for Disease Control in other countries.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To consolidate these capabilities and expertise, we will take the next step to set up a dedicated centre for public health, similar to what many other countries have done in setting up Centres for Disease Control.

sections.label: Pandemic planning baseline scenarios
sections.summary: A pathogen with high mortality and high contagion risk requires broadening baseline pandemic planning scenarios and reviewing needed resources.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The more dangerous scenario will be one where we have a pathogen that has both high mortality and high contagion risk.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will need to broaden the range of baseline scenarios for pandemic planning and review the resources we need to respond to these different scenarios.

sections.label: Preparedness and improvisation balance
sections.summary: Limited resources require balancing contingencies that can be pivoted just in time, combining preparedness and improvisation.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, we will have to strike the right balance to make good use of our limited resources.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This may involve planning for contingencies that can be pivoted “just in time” to support our pandemic response, so we do not have to build layers of redundancies that may remain underused outside of a crisis but cost us a disproportionate amount of resources to maintain.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In other words, our response will have to be a combination of preparedness and improvisation.

sections.label: Forward planning team for pandemics
sections.summary: Past forward planning competed with operational demands, so future pandemics will have a dedicated forward planning team.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, whatever forward planning capacity we had competed with operational demands for resources and mindshare.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And again, learning from this, in future pandemics, we will set up a dedicated forward planning team with the bandwidth and expertise to look ahead.

sections.label: Stockpiling and supply chain efforts
sections.summary: Minister Gan Kim Yong will elaborate on stockpiling, supply chain diversification and local production expansion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Minister Gan Kim Yong will elaborate on these efforts, including our stockpiling strategies, diversification of supply chains for essential items and expansion of local production where this makes sense.

sections.label: Multi-use government facilities
sections.summary: The Government will design facilities to be multi-use so they can be repurposed during a crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Where possible, the Government will design facilities to be multi-use, so they can be repurposed or redeployed during a crisis.

sections.label: Financial Reserves in pandemic response
sections.summary: Financial Reserves were a crucial resource that enabled effective response and quick recovery in this pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: One crucial resource that enabled us to respond effectively and bounce back quickly in this pandemic was our financial Reserves.

sections.label: Unity lesson from COVID-19
sections.summary: The next pandemic may be sooner and worse, so Singaporeans must stay united as One People and One Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The next pandemic can happen sooner rather than later, and quite possibly, will be worse than COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Let us always remember the most important lesson of COVID-19, that we are stronger when we stand and work together.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Let us resolve to stay united, so that whatever the challenges ahead, we can overcome them as One People and One Singapore.

sections.label: Post-election COVID-19 parliamentary measures
sections.summary: Post-elections, COVID-19-specific measures were raised in Parliament on adverse events, controls, vaccination, TraceTogether and migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Post-elections, we raised COVID-19-specific measures in Parliament covering a wide range of issues, such as the MOH's suspected adverse events report, recalibration of COVID-19 controls for Singaporeans visiting their terminally-ill family members, vaccination safety protocols for children, clarifying the Government's position on TraceTogether with regard to its applicability for criminal investigations, the inclusion of non-mRNA vaccines into the National Vaccination Programme and the reasons behind the delay in permitting migrant workers to be reintegrated into the community, just to name a few.

sections.label: COVID-19 After Action Review White Paper
sections.summary: The House was told Mr Peter Ho oversaw the COVID-19 After Action Review, and the White Paper draws on his review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On 9 May 2022, in response to my Parliamentary Question, this House was informed that the former Head of Civil Service, Mr Peter Ho, was overseeing the COVID-19 After Action Review (AAR) process and that the Government would share the findings and lessons with the public when the AAR was completed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To that end, the White Paper tabled before the House today states that it “was prepared by the Prime Minister’s Office” and that it draws on Mr Ho's review, which included interviews with key participants in the crisis, both Ministers and civil servants.

sections.label: Publishing Peter Ho review report
sections.summary: The speaker asks why the Government did not publish Mr Peter Ho's original review report in full.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Why did the Government decide against publishing the original review report presented by Mr Peter Ho in full?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To publish the original AAR report would be consistent with the spirit of the Motion, which seeks to affirm the Government's effort to learn from the experiences of the last three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I will speak on what the WP did and deliberately did not do during COVID-19.

sections.label: WP conduct during COVID-19
sections.summary: WP members donated to the Courage Fund and WP called for unity and politics to take a backseat during COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Other WP members and volunteers donated generously to the Courage Fund under the National Council for Social Services which sought to provide support to lower-income households affected by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It seems a long time ago now, but, as early as February 2020, when the Unity Budget was announced, the WP made clear the tone we would take on the COVID-19 crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We called for a unity of purpose and for politics to take a backseat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In June 2020, as we exited the circuit breaker, and a few weeks before the elections, I reiterated in my speech on the Fortitude Budget, that the WP did not come in to publicly criticise the Government on its handling of an unprecedented crisis.

sections.label: Solidarity and vaccine injury claims
sections.summary: The speaker stands in solidarity with those affected by COVID-19 and hopes MOH follows up on unsuccessful vaccine injury claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We also stand in solidarity with Singaporeans and our non-Singaporean friends who have lost family members to COVID-19 and to those who suffer from COVID-19 or vaccine-related ailments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I hope the MOH will proactively follow-up with all individuals who have not succeeded in their vaccine injury claims and consider their circumstances and the well-being of their mental health, as appropriate, on an ongoing basis.

sections.label: National Wages Council convened twice
sections.summary: The National Wages Council was convened twice in 2020 when the economy deteriorated rapidly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The National Wages Council (NWC) was convened twice in 2020 when the economy deteriorated rapidly.

sections.label: NTUC Job Security Council
sections.summary: NTUC developed the Job Security Council in 2020 to achieve this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: NTUC developed the Job Security Council (JSC) in 2020 to achieve this.

sections.label: Worker redeployment to healthcare
sections.summary: The programme deployed workers from hard-hit sectors like aviation to healthcare roles such as Care Ambassadors in hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Through this programme, workers in hard-hit sectors like aviation were deployed to the healthcare sector, transferring their knowledge by performing roles like Care Ambassadors in the hospitals.

sections.label: JSC secondment with FDAWU
sections.summary: The JSC worked with FDAWU and RC Hotels to place Gina on secondment to NTUC FairPrice as a retail assistant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The JSC worked with the Food, Drinks and Allied Workers Union (FDAWU) and RC Hotels, Gina’s employer, to place her on secondment to NTUC FairPrice, where she took on a retail assistant role.

sections.label: JSC job matches since pandemic
sections.summary: As of February 2023, the JSC has matched about 70,000 workers to new jobs since the pandemic started.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: As of February 2023, the JSC has matched about 70,000 workers to new jobs since the pandemic started.

sections.label: JSS saved local jobs
sections.summary: JSS helped retain local employees, with an estimated 165,000 local jobs saved from March to December 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: It helped them to retain local employees during the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: It was estimated that 165,000 local jobs were saved from March to December 2020 because of JSS.

sections.label: SEP payout scheme
sections.summary: The scheme helped some 200,000 SEPs obtain $9,000 to tide through the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The scheme was able to help some 200,000 SEPs to obtain $9,000 to tide through the pandemic.

sections.label: Short-term income support for SEPs
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to develop short-term income support for SEPs tied to training and job search.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: During periods of business or income disruptions, SEPs also need access to short-term income support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: I call upon the Government to look into developing such support which can be tied to their efforts to train and search for jobs.

sections.label: COVID-19 deaths in Singapore
sections.summary: COVID-19 took the lives of over 1,700 people in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: COVID-19 also took the lives of over 1,700 people in Singapore.

sections.label: Emergency department waiting times
sections.summary: Median waiting times for emergency cases requiring hospital admission from January to September last year was about seven hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, median waiting times for emergency cases that require hospital admission from January to September last year was about seven hours.

sections.label: Nurse resignations in 2021
sections.summary: In 2021, 7.4% of local nurses and 14.8% of foreign nurses resigned, a five-year high.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2021, the proportion of nurses resigning hit a five-year high, with 7.4% of local nurses and 14.8% of foreign nurses leaving their jobs.

sections.label: UK nurses and Advance Practice Nurses
sections.summary: In the UK, nurses run clinics, diagnose patients, take management roles and lead research, and Singapore should accelerate reaching 700 Advance Practice Nurses by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the UK, nurses run clinics, diagnose patients, take on high-level management roles and help to lead medical research.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We should accelerate efforts to achieve the target of 700 Advance Practice Nurses by 2030.

sections.label: SafeEntry scanning difficulties
sections.summary: Many wheelchair users and people with developmental disabilities, visual impairments and autism spectrum disorder had difficulties with SafeEntry scanning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Many wheelchair users and people with developmental disabilities, visual impairments and autism spectrum disorder had difficulties with SafeEntry scanning.

sections.label: January 2020 mask advisory
sections.summary: In January 2020, the Government issued an infographic saying masks are generally not needed for well people and that mask stockpiles were sufficient.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In January 2020, the Government issued an infographic titled "Advisory on wearing masks" which highlighted that "masks are generally not needed for people who are well." The infographic, which was also posted on social media, added that "there are sufficient masks in the warehouses and Government stockpiles." The then-chairman of the PAP's Government Parliamentary Committee for Health, Dr Chia Shi-Lu, echoed the Government's line later that month when he told the New Paper that "surgical masks can prevent the passing of virus from a wearer, but when it comes to protecting (a healthy wearer), the masks won't protect from viruses." The Prime Minister, in January 2020, said Singaporeans should follow doctors' advice on how best to protect themselves from the virus, which includes not wearing a mask when they are unwell.

sections.label: Face mask advice and trust
sections.summary: The White Paper said the Government could have encouraged Singaporeans to devise their own face masks, and public trust was eroded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The White Paper stated that "in hindsight…the Government could have encouraged Singaporeans to devise their own face masks while we set up manufacturing lines to ramp up production of surgical masks." This was not hindsight – it was what the four doctors advised in the first place, which the Government did not heed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The result of this about-turn, as acknowledged by the White Paper, was that public trust in the Government was eroded.

sections.label: US Defense Production Act legislation
sections.summary: It asks whether the Government will consider legislation like the US Defense Production Act to direct private companies and restrict hoarding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Will the Government consider legislation akin to the US Defense Production Act, which empowers the executive to direct private companies to prioritise orders from the federal government and take actions to restrict the hoarding of needed supplies?

sections.label: Temasek COVID-19 spending question
sections.summary: It asks how much Temasek and related organisations spent from their own budgets on COVID-19 initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: During Question Time on 3 March, I asked Senior Minister of State for Finance Chee Hong Tat if the Government's total COVID-19 spending of $72.3 billion included the amount spent by Temasek Holdings, Temasek Foundation and other Temasek-linked companies for their COVID-19 activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Senior Minister of State gave a rather convoluted answer, but I believe the answer was no.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This being the case, can I ask – how much did Temasek and its related organisations spend out of their own budgets on COVID-19 initiatives like face masks, hand sanitisers and oxygen concentrators, which were made available locally and overseas?

sections.label: Temasek spending and Reserves
sections.summary: It asks whether Temasek's COVID-19 expenditure draws on Reserves and whether the President's approval was sought and obtained.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I appreciate the work that Temasek companies and their employees did to keep Singaporeans safe during the pandemic and the resources they spent doing so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But I think it is important for the House to know if Temasek's expenditure on COVID-19 constitutes a draw on our Reserves and, if so, whether the approval of the President was sought and obtained?

sections.label: New dormitory standards
sections.summary: It lists new standards including a maximum of 12 residents per room and extension of the Foreign Employee Dormitories Act to smaller dormitories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Our new standards include a maximum of 12 residents in a room, en-suite toilets, no more than six residents to one toilet, adequate fans, more spacious rooms, adequate space between beds and even in-room Wi-Fi.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am also glad that our Foreign Employee Dormitories Act has been extended from larger dormitories with 1,000 or more workers to smaller dormitories with seven beds or more.

sections.label: Electronic salary payments
sections.summary: By January 2021, 97% of all employers were paying salaries electronically.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: By January 2021, 97% of all employers were paying salaries electronically.

sections.label: Mandating electronic payment for work permit holders
sections.summary: The speaker calls for mandating electronic payment for all work permit holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Let us go the further step and mandate electronic payment for all work permit holders.

sections.label: Civil society support for migrant workers
sections.summary: Civil society provided material items and emotional support, and regular Government-NGO sharing sessions worked towards improving migrant worker conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Civil society truly stepped up to provide material items from masks, sanitisers, daily necessities and food to the less tangible but no less important needs such as mental wellness helplines and other initiatives to provide emotional and psychological support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Regular sharing sessions between the Government and NGOs ensured that we could work in tandem towards the common goal of improving conditions for our migrant workers.

sections.label: Continuing migrant worker improvements without another pandemic
sections.summary: The speaker hopes efforts to improve living conditions, enforce electronic payment and sustain civil society partnership continue without waiting for another pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: These were issues that civil society has called for, for many years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope these efforts continue and we do not wait for another pandemic to further improve living conditions, enforce electronic payment for all workers and sustain partnership with civil society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Another pandemic is too high a price for us to pay to learn the lessons again.

sections.label: JSS wage support for businesses
sections.summary: JSS provided wage support so companies could retain employees and keep most businesses afloat during the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: JSS was critical in keeping most businesses afloat during the pandemic and preserving jobs for workers by providing wage support for the companies to retain employees.

sections.label: Singapore Rediscover vouchers and hotel rooms
sections.summary: STB's Singapore Rediscover vouchers helped hotels retain local workforce, SHA hotel members stayed at 160, and over half of 67,000 hotel rooms were used against COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Additionally, the launch of STB's Singapore Rediscover vouchers in December 2020 was another scheme which helped hotels to keep the lights on and retain its local workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The SHA would like to record its appreciation to the Government for helping the industry stay resilient.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, the number of SHA hotel members has remained unchanged from pre-COVID-19 days at 160." Hon Members of this House, many of us would recall ourselves or loved ones having to stay away from home while serving isolation, quarantine or Stay-Home Notice (SHN).

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Isolation, quarantine and SHN was an important line of defence against the pandemic and, at one point, more than half of the 67,000 hotel rooms in Singapore at that time were used in our battle against COVID-19.

sections.label: White Paper and migrant worker healthcare
sections.summary: The White Paper was objective and frank on issues and lessons, and MOM set up a new primary healthcare system with six medical centres for migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In hindsight, much could have been done differently by everyone, and the White Paper was objective and frank in calling out the issues and the lessons learnt." As we read in the White Paper, MOM has since set up a new primary healthcare system for migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are now six medical centres for migrant workers across the island.

sections.label: Public transport during pandemic
sections.summary: At the pandemic peak, daily ridership fell below 25% of pre-COVID-19 levels, but bus and MRT service levels were sustained at largely pre-COVID-19 frequencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the peak of the pandemic, average daily ridership dropped to less than 25% of pre-COVID-19, but it was decided that public transport must be kept available for our essential workers and bus and MRT train service levels were sustained at largely pre-COVID-19 frequencies.

sections.label: Suspension of long-term passholders
sections.summary: Singapore temporarily suspended entry of long-term passholders, generally family members of tax-paying Employment Pass holders, causing a PR hit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For all the positives of how well Singapore has managed during COVID-19, there was one low light besides the dormitories that caused us a PR hit and the Deputy Prime Minister mentioned it just now as well.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There were various points in time when Singapore temporarily suspended the entry of long-term passholders, who are, generally, the family members of tax-paying Employment Pass (EP) holders.

sections.label: SBF placements under programme
sections.summary: SBF approved and onboarded around 19,500 placements from May 2020 to December 2022, about 10% of total placements in the White Paper.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SBF was one of the administrators for the programme and approved and onboarded around 19,500 placements from May 2020 to December 2022, about 10% of the total placements as reported in the White Paper.

sections.label: Singapore Polytechnic SGUnited participation
sections.summary: Singapore Polytechnic trained about 1,200 jobseekers, hired over 100 trainees under SGUnited Traineeship, and seven trainees later got employment contracts with SP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore Polytechnic (SP), which I am involved with, participated actively in supporting the SGUnited skills programmes, training about 1,200 jobseekers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SP itself hired more than 100 of the trainees under the SGUnited Traineeship (SGUT) Programme and put the trainees to work in producing online videos to support the home-based learning during COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When the traineeship was over, seven of the trainees got employment contracts with SP.

sections.label: Singapore unity during COVID-19
sections.summary: Singapore can rise above troubles if people stand together, SG United, as during COVID-19, to handle the next crisis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore, once again can rise above these troubles if we, like during COVID-19, stand together, shoulder to shoulder, hand-in-hand, SG United and resolved to handle whatever this next crisis lies ahead of us with strength, with hope and with love for our country.

sections.label: Supply chains as lifeline
sections.summary: Supply chains for masks, gloves, PPE, oxygen, ventilators and medications are the lifeline and battle armour for healthcare frontliners, needing uninterrupted readiness.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Our supply chains are our lifeline, whether it is face masks, surgical gloves or personal protective equipment (PPE), whether it is oxygen supplies, ventilators, or medications.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: These are the battle armour and ammunition that our healthcare frontliners used to protect and save Singaporean lives.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: These supplies need to be ready and they need to be uninterrupted, going beyond just-in-time delivery and moving towards preparing for just-in-case.

sections.label: Gazetting essential supplies as state property
sections.summary: He asked whether MOH works with MinLaw and AGC to study gazetting purchased essential supplies as sovereign state property while still in overseas suppliers' warehouses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I asked this two weeks ago, during the MOH debate on the Budget.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I asked whether MOH is working together with the Ministry of Law (MinLaw) and the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) to study whether certain essential supplies required for our survival, whether such supplies, once the purchase is done, can these supplies be gazetted as sovereign state property at that moment, even if the items are still in the suppliers' warehouse overseas.

sections.label: Singapore vaccine research and production capability
sections.summary: He asked whether Singapore can research, develop and produce a new vaccine on shore through its own companies or international partners.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: If there needs to be a new vaccine against a new COVID-19 variant or a new pandemic, does Singapore have the capability to research, develop, produce the vaccine on shore, either through our own companies or through international partners working with us, based on Singapore's soil?

sections.label: Metagenomics for early pandemic detection
sections.summary: He asked MOH in October 2021 about metagenomics, sequencing environmental and sewage DNA to detect a new pandemic early.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In October 2021, I asked MOH on the use of metagenomics.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: You take samples from the environment – whether it is surfaces, sewage and so on – you then sequence all the DNA, both what is known and unknown, and if the pattern of that metagenomics study, if the pattern of DNA in the environment and the sewage changes at the same time as many people are falling ill, that could be an early indicator of a new pandemic.

sections.label: COVID-19 bonus for outsourced healthcare cleaners
sections.summary: He said outsourced cleaners in restructured hospitals missed the 2020 COVID-19 bonus, and the Minister later confirmed the Healthcare Award covered outsourced frontline workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Same job, same workplace, same COVID-19 risks, different contracts and now outsourced to a service provider.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: But looking back, in 2020, the then Finance Minister had stated in the Budget debate round-up speech, "The Government will award public officers on the frontline who are directly battling with the COVID-19 disease up to one additional month of special bonus.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: This will include many healthcare officers in MOH and the restructured hospitals." But as I pointed out in Parliament in February 2021, there were Clementi residents and brothers and sisters in the Labour Movement who found that some cleaners serving in restructured hospitals did not qualify for this bonus because their contracts were outsourced.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Later that year, in November 2021 and in reply to my January 2022 Parliamentary Question and my March 2022 questions to MOH during the Budget debate, the Minister for Health confirmed that the subsequent COVID-19 Healthcare Award for "all staff of public healthcare institutions" would include frontline healthcare workers from outsourced service providers serving at public healthcare institutions.

sections.label: Same job, same workplace, same risk
sections.summary: He stated that on the pandemic frontline, the same job and workplace means the same risk even if the contract says the worker is outsourced.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Second, on the pandemic frontline – same job, same workplace means same risk, even if the contract looks different and says the worker is outsourced.

sections.label: Healthcare team based in one institution
sections.summary: He stated that in a COVID-19 world the healthcare team is better based within the same institution rather than moving between hospitals under outsourced arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In a COVID-19 world, it is better for the healthcare team to be all based within the same healthcare institution rather than moving between different hospitals, as may happen with an outsourced arrangement.

sections.label: Post-COVID resilience review call
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to review lessons from COVID-19, moving from efficiency towards resilience.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It sent a message that you are part of the same team, you are shouldering the same risk as everyone else, you are one of us, and we are together.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, I call upon the Government to look seriously at this as part of the post-COVID-19 review and the lessons from COVID-19 for governments around the world because it is part of how we think, how we think beyond pure efficiency, "just in time" towards resilience "just in case".

sections.label: Wage support to businesses
sections.summary: $30 billion was distributed to businesses in wage support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, $30 billion was distributed to businesses in wage support.

sections.label: Reserves draw and GST
sections.summary: $30 billion equals 17% of GST collection, and the $40 billion draw from past Reserves is unlikely to be paid back.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Thirty billion dollars is a big amount and equivalent to a GST collection of 17%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Deputy Prime Minister has told us that the $40 billion draw from our past Reserves is unlikely to be paid back.

sections.label: Vaccination rates and reservations
sections.summary: Falling from over 90% full vaccination to 60% up-to-date shows the true level of reservations on vaccination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: From a full vaccination rate of over 90% to the 60% up-to-date vaccination rate, we can see the true level of reservations on vaccination.

sections.label: Roadmap for future restrictions
sections.summary: The speaker believes the July 2021 call remains relevant and a roadmap with support measures pegged to restriction levels should be developed.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It was also a source of great frustration for businesses and organisations that they often had to wait a few days for rules that were specific to their sector to be announced.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I, therefore, believe the call we made in July 2021 is still relevant and that we should ensure that we develop a roadmap for future use, clearly laying out support measures pegged to specific restriction levels.

sections.label: Agencies sharing quarantine information
sections.summary: The speaker suggests improving structures so agencies integrate information smoothly, after quarantine feedback about repeated calls for the same information.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Still on communications, one area which we perhaps could look into is to work out a system of improving our existing structures to ensure that our agencies are able to more smoothly integrate the information they have and to be efficient in processing this.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I make this comment after receiving feedback from residents and friends who were subject to quarantine orders, who told me that they often received numerous calls from different departments of various Ministries, each asking them for the exact same information which they had already provided.

sections.label: Youth well-being and White Paper
sections.summary: 38% of youths aged 15 to 19 reported drops in quality of life, yet the White Paper scantily mentions well-being and mental health.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Likewise, 38% of youths aged 15 to 19 reported drops in the quality of life, compared with 28% for the general population.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet, there has been scant mention of well-being and mental health in the White Paper.

sections.label: Long COVID prevalence estimates
sections.summary: A Lancet meta-analysis found 45% of patients had unresolved symptoms four months post-infection, with 65 million people worldwide estimated to have long COVID.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Indeed, a recent meta-analysis published in The Lancet even seems to have found a worrying 45% of patients, regardless of hospitalisation status, still suffer from unresolved symptoms four months post-infection.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Indeed, The Lancet also recently estimated, too, that approximately 65 million people worldwide are estimated to struggle with "long COVID" and that one in 10 people with "long COVID" stop working.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given that we have reported more than 2.2 million COVID-19 cases, even a small percentage of this would be significant.

sections.label: Singapore employer long COVID support
sections.summary: Mercer Marsh Benefits found Singapore ranks lowest in Asia for employer help adjusting jobs for employees with long COVID.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Equally alarming, too, is the finding by Mercer Marsh Benefits that Singapore ranks lowest in Asia for help given by employers to make adjustments to the job to cater to employees suffering from "long COVID".

sections.label: COVID-19 antiviral subsidies and charges
sections.summary: COVID-19 antivirals like Paxlovid remain fully subsidised for clinically eligible outpatients, while hospitals will start charging for these medications.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In particular, COVID-19 antivirals, such as Paxlovid, will remain fully subsidised for clinically eligible patients in outpatient settings.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I further understand that hospitals will now start to charge for these important medications.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Would the Minister be able to confirm that this is, indeed, the case and to explain the rationale behind such a move?

sections.label: Thanking pandemic heroes and lessons
sections.summary: The speaker thanks everyday heroes for post-pandemic freedoms and hopes they are valued and lessons implemented in future crises.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I am forever thankful for how you cheerfully suited up each time so that you could hold him and try to calm him while I snatched precious moments, seconds, to use the toilet.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We owe our post-pandemic freedoms today to our everyday heroes and I hope that we do right by them in repaying the debt that we owe them by valuing them in concrete ways and also by ensuring that the sacrifices made and lessons learnt along the way are implemented in any future public health crisis that we face.

sections.label: WHO role in pandemic response
sections.summary: The speaker acknowledges international bodies like WHO in shaping pandemic response, adopting measures including mask-wearing and border restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, Mr Speaker, Sir, on healthcare-related measures, it is important to acknowledge the roles of international bodies, such as the World Health Organization (WHO), in shaping our pandemic response.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We adopted many WHO-recommended measures, including mask-wearing and border restrictions.

sections.label: Vaccine approval and local research
sections.summary: Asks how Singapore can hasten vaccine approval for future pandemics and support local research like the Arcturus and Duke-NUS COVID-19 vaccine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How can Singapore further hasten the process of vaccine approval for future pandemics, learning from the COVID-19 experience?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How can we also support our local research and developments, like the COVID-19 vaccine that was developed by Arcturus Therapeutics and Duke-NUS?

sections.label: MOM retrenchment compliance
sections.summary: Asks how MOM ensured compliance, or whether legislation should have made retrenchments a last resort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How did the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) ensure compliance or should we have done more, like move legislation, to ensure that retrenchments were necessary and done as a last resort?

sections.label: Frontline workers and GP clinics
sections.summary: Registers gratitude to frontline workers and notes about 1,800 GP clinics provide around 80% of primary healthcare, with enhanced roles under Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On that note, I would like to register, alongside all Members of this House, a profound debt of gratitude that we all owe to the frontline workers who toiled at the coalface of this crisis – healthcare workers and many other frontline staff – without whose sacrifice we would have, collectively, paid a much higher price.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There are about 1,800 GP clinics in Singapore providing around 80% of primary healthcare services to our citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the newly-launched Healthier SG, the role of GPs will be enhanced to become more proactive on the preventive healthcare front.

sections.label: Migrant worker dormitory outbreak
sections.summary: States the COVID-19 outbreak in migrant workers' dormitories will remain a blight on Singapore's pandemic report card.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The COVID-19 outbreak in the migrant workers' dormitories in Singapore will remain a blight on the report card in the way Singapore managed the pandemic.

sections.label: TWC2 flagged outbreak early
sections.summary: States the NGO Transient Workers Count Too flagged the oncoming train as early as 23 March 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The light of the oncoming train was flagged out by the NGO Transient Workers Count Too (TWC2) as early as 23 March 2020.

sections.label: Dormitory standards and enforcement
sections.summary: States that despite MOM announcing improved dormitory standards, migrant worker anecdotes show uneven enforcement for smaller dormitories and no timeline for purpose-built dormitories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Despite the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) announcing improved standards for dormitories, anecdotes from migrant workers on the ground show that there is uneven enforcement for the smaller dormitories and there is no timeline yet for the purpose-built dormitories which meet these standards.

sections.label: Migrant worker movement restrictions ended
sections.summary: All movement restrictions for migrant workers were wound down on 1 March this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: All movement restrictions were only wound down for migrant workers on 1 March this year.

sections.label: Dormitory mental health and outbreak plans
sections.summary: A 2021 TODAY report linked complete restrictions to mental health burden, prompting questions on national rollout of improved dormitory standards, NEST's role, and outbreak plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A report in the media outlet TODAY in August 2021 read: "The large number of mental health symptoms reported among workers under complete restrictions suggests that while isolation of whole facilities may be expedient for limiting COVID-19 transmission, this comes at the cost of an increased mental health burden, researchers said." Hence, I would like to ask what is the timeline for the improved standards in migrant worker dormitories to be rolled out nationally, including the role of NEST?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And will the Government build on this unfortunate experience to develop a clear plan to manage a major infectious disease outbreak in migrant worker dormitories, with all of the massive logistical challenges that will entail?

sections.label: Singapore psychologist and psychiatrist ratios
sections.summary: The Government revealed Singapore has 9.7 psychologists per 100,000 population, compared with around 30 in the US and 49 in Canada and France, and under five psychiatrists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In reply to a Parliamentary Question from Sengkang Member of Parliament, Ms He Ting Ru, the Government revealed that our number of psychologists per 100,000 of our population is 9.7.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This compares to around 30 in the US and 49 in Canada and France, for example.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The same ratio for psychiatrists places Singapore under five, versus, for example, 15 for Canada and 24 for Finland.

sections.label: Publishing Peter Ho AAR report
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government will make public the original internal AAR report by Mr Peter Ho and his team, with redactions for national security or commercial sensitivities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the spirit of these observations and to reiterate the arguments put forth by the Leader of the Opposition on this very same point, I hope the Government would consider making public the original internal AAR report developed by Mr Peter Ho and his team, with redactions as regards any matters pertaining to national security or which have commercial sensitivities.

sections.label: Lessons from migrant dormitory crisis
sections.summary: The speaker highlights five lessons from the dormitory crisis, focusing on smaller FCDs housing a third of 300,000 workers, poor conditions, FEDA regulation, and four proposed conditions.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: For all the good work that was done, I understand that the Government's motivation for the White Paper is not so much a pat on the back, but to bring light to blind spots so that Singapore will bounce back stronger in our next crisis.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: I wish to highlight five lessons and actions for consideration from the migrant workers' dormitory crisis, with a focus on the smaller FCDs that house a third of the 300,000 workers staying in the dormitories.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: The COVID-19 crisis in the dormitories was perpetuated due to the poor living conditions.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: This is most evident in the smaller FCDs that were not regulated by the Foreign Employee Dormitories Act (FEDA).

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: In July 2016, the Migrant Workers' Centre had published photos of the poor housing and hygiene conditions of some of the FCDs and flagged the issue to MOM.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: The four conditions include: (a) the provision of feedback channel for workers to report issues related to the housing conditions of FCDs; (b) provision of personal locker for each worker; (c) provision of at least one sick bay in the FCD – alternatively, the operator can develop a contingency plan to deal with cases of infectious diseases; and lastly (d) provision of Wi-Fi within the FCD.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: If a contingency plan for infectious diseases was indeed in place, could the COVID-19 crisis have been better dealt within the FCDs?

sections.label: Food supply to migrant workers
sections.summary: Some migrant workers went without food for two to three days before NGOs found them, and meals were supplied to FCDs for eight to 12 weeks before NGOs stopped.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Some migrant workers had been without food for two to three days before the NGOs found them.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Meals were supplied to the FCDs for an extended time period between eight and 12 weeks before NGOs put a hard stop to food supply after informing MOM, calling for employers to be responsible for their workers.

sections.label: Employers flagging help in crisis
sections.summary: It asks what means exist for employers with genuine needs to flag for help during a crisis so workers are not left to fend for themselves due to cost pressures.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: First, what are the available means by which employers with genuine needs could flag for help during a crisis so that workers are not left to fend for themselves due to cost pressures?

sections.label: NGO coordination and five calls
sections.summary: It notes NGOs overserved some dormitories and underserved others without a coordinating body, and lists five calls: MOM enforcement, employer accountability, migrant worker inclusion in crisis communication, identifying multinational representatives, and NGO resource coordination.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Given the scale of the dormitory crisis, many NGOs and informal groups stepped forward to serve the workers in whatever way they could and wherever they saw need.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, the NGOs had observed that this led to some dormitories being overserved and others underserved as there was no coordinating body across the NGOs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: To close and summarise, my speech calls for five things for us to learn from and act on: first, MOM's enforcement of regulations to improve living conditions in FCDs; second, accountability of employers of migrant workers residing in FCDs; third, inclusion of the migrant worker community in crisis communication; four, identifying multinational representatives within dormitories; and fifth, coordination of NGO resources during crises.

sections.label: Securing vulnerable migrant workers' safety
sections.summary: It states Singapore is positioned to win a pandemic war when the safety of the most vulnerable is secured, and calls for closing migrant workers' health and safety gaps.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: In a war against all or any pandemic, Singapore is positioned to win when we secure the safety of those most vulnerable among us.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Let us close the health and safety gaps of our migrant workers and see Singapore win in the next pandemic.

sections.label: Inter-agency Task Force set up
sections.summary: It states the Government set up the Inter-agency Task Force in April 2020, brought in the SAF, Home Team and public healthcare, mobilised nearly 3,000 officers and volunteers, and put dormitories under lockdown with the circuit breaker.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Recognising the scale of the outbreak in the dormitories, the Government set up the Inter-agency Task Force (ITF) in April 2020, brought in the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) and the Home Team, as well as public healthcare capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Drawing on the expertise and resources of multiple stakeholders, the ITF mobilised nearly 3,000 officers and volunteers from the SAF, the Home Team, MOM and across the Public Service.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In April 2020, the dormitories were progressively put under lockdown and the circuit breaker was also implemented in the community.

sections.label: ITF sets up medical posts
sections.summary: It states that after the difficult decision, the ITF swung into action and set up medical posts and networks in and around the dormitories.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Once we had made that difficult decision, the ITF swung into action and set up medical posts and networks in and around the dormitories.

sections.label: Meals distributed, workers kept apart
sections.summary: It states workers could not intermingle within dormitories to slow virus transmission, meals were organised and distributed to 200,000 workers over four months, and employers continued paying workers who could not work.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: To slow down the transmission of the virus in the dormitories, the workers could not intermingle within the dormitories.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We organised and we distributed the meals to the 200,000 workers over four months and ensured that employers continued to pay their workers even when they could not work.

sections.label: Dormitory lockdown lifted, infections estimated
sections.summary: When the dormitory lockdown was lifted in August 2020, about half of migrant workers in dormitories were estimated to have been infected, mostly mildly or asymptomatically.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: By the time that the dormitory lockdown was lifted in August 2020, we estimated that about half of the migrant workers in dormitories had been infected by COVID-19, the vast majority of whom had mild or asymptomatic infection.

sections.label: ITF testing and ACE Group
sections.summary: By August 2020 the ITF had tested all dormitory residents to clear dormitories, and the ACE Group in MOM was formed to continue its work.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: By August 2020, the ITF had completed testing of all dormitory residents to clear the dormitories of COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: To continue the work of the ITF, the Assurance, Care and Engagement (ACE) Group in MOM was formed.

sections.label: Zero new dormitory cases
sections.summary: ACE and MOH controlled post-clearance clusters through testing and isolation, reaching zero new dormitory cases on 13 October 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Even though there were some COVID-19 clusters and transmission after the completion of dormitory clearance, ACE and MOH working closely together, were able to bring these under control through testing and through isolation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We achieved a significant milestone of zero new cases reported in the dormitories on 13 October 2020.

sections.label: Migrant worker vaccination and Delta
sections.summary: In under six months over nine in 10 dormitory migrant workers were fully vaccinated, and no further loss of life occurred when Delta struck in mid-2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In less than six months, over nine in 10 migrant workers living in the dormitories were fully vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This made a difference when the highly transmissible Delta variant struck in mid-2021 and there was no further loss of life to COVID-19 among migrant workers living in the dormitories.

sections.label: Improved dormitory standards introduced
sections.summary: In September 2021 improved standards were introduced for all new migrant worker dormitories.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In September 2021, we introduced improved standards for all new migrant worker dormitories.

sections.label: FEDA scope expanded
sections.summary: From 1 April 2023 FEDA's scope expands to dormitories with seven or more beds, raising regulated dormitories from 53 to 1,500.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The scope of the Foreign Employee Dormitories Act (FEDA) will be expanded to include migrant worker dormitories with seven or more beds starting from 1 April 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This will increase the number of dormitories, including FCDs, regulated under FEDA from the current 53, in about two weeks' time, it will go up to 1,500, and allow MOM to raise standards and respond quickly to future emergencies.

sections.label: MOM building two new dormitories
sections.summary: MOM will build and own two new dormitories operated by a new corporate entity with the private sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: To grow our capabilities in dormitory management, MOM will also be building and owning two new dormitories, which will be operated by a new corporate entity in partnership with the private sector.

sections.label: Primary Care Plan for workers
sections.summary: A Primary Care Plan offered by all Anchor Operators covers most primary care needs at a fixed annual fee to employers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For the second initiative, we have also mandated a Primary Care Plan (PCP) offered by all Anchor Operators that covers most of the primary care needs of the workers at a fixed annual fee to employers, thereby giving them greater peace of mind.

sections.label: Project DAWN for migrant workers
sections.summary: Project DAWN comprises MOM, Government, psychologists, IMH and two NGOs to manage and support migrant workers' mental health.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We could have eased up more quickly, but, then again, all this is on hindsight.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This comprises representatives from MOM, the Government, psychologists, the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) and two NGOs – the Migrant Workers' Centre (MWC) and HealthServe.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The purpose of forming Project DAWN is to develop a comprehensive support ecosystem to manage and support the mental health of migrant workers.

sections.label: HealthServe 24-hour counselling hotline
sections.summary: With MOM's support, HealthServe set up a 24-hour counselling hotline operational since August 2021 and hired native-speaking para-counsellors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: With MOM's support, HealthServe set up its 24-hour counselling hotline which has been operational since August 2021 and hired more native-speaking para-counsellors to deliver culturally attuned counselling.

sections.label: National Jobs Council and SGUnited Package
sections.summary: The National Jobs Council was formed to oversee the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package supporting locals to enter jobs or upskill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: To expand opportunities for jobseekers amid uncertainty and disruptions, the National Jobs Council (NJC) was formed to oversee the design and implementation of the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package, which supported locals to enter new jobs, to upskill themselves, or to be better positioned for recovery.

sections.label: Local placements and hiring support
sections.summary: From April 2020 to April 2022, around 200,000 locals were placed into jobs and skills opportunities under the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: From April 2020 to April 2022, around 200,000 locals were placed into jobs and skills opportunities under the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Besides, over 744,000 jobseekers were hired with support under the Jobs Growth Incentive, which encouraged local hiring in growing firms as the focus shifted to supporting recovery.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Close to 200,000 self-employed persons benefited from SIRS.

sections.label: Resident employment rebound 2020
sections.summary: By December 2020 resident employment was slightly above pre-COVID-19 levels, with 14,900 more residents employed that year despite first-half contractions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: By December 2020, resident employment had rebounded to slightly above pre-COVID-19 levels, with the net number of residents in employment for the year increasing by 14,900, despite contractions in the first half of 2020.

sections.label: COVID-19 illness and recession
sections.summary: 2.2 million people fell ill, and 2020 brought the worst full-year recession since Independence, with a 13.2% second-quarter contraction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In all, 2.2 million people fell ill to the disease.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In 2020, we suffered the worst full-year recession since our Independence, where in the second quarter of that year, the economy contracted by a hefty 13.2%.

sections.label: Pandemic Parliament measures and Reserves
sections.summary: Measures included spaced seating, masks, microphone wiping, antigen rapid tests, five Budgets in a year and $37 billion drawn from the Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We had to sit wide apart – using up the gallery spaces up there, wearing masks, wiping the microphones and rostrum after each speech and conducting self-antigen rapid tests (ART).

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We even had five Budgets in a year and drawn on an unprecedented amount of $37 billion from the Reserves.

sections.label: Post-SARS capabilities built
sections.summary: Key successes included capabilities built up post-SARS, namely the National Public Health Laboratory and the National Centre for Infectious Diseases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Among the key successes were the capabilities that we have built up post-SARs, namely the National Public Health Laboratory (NPHL) and the National Centre for Infectious Diseases (NCID).

sections.label: Domestic mask demand scale
sections.summary: Domestic demand for masks in a non-pandemic environment is not high enough for production to achieve viable scale efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Our domestic demand for masks under a non-pandemic environment is not high enough to achieve the scale efficiency for production to be viable.

sections.label: Medical masks as critical supply
sections.summary: To prepare for future pandemics, medical masks must be designated a critical supply item requiring some local production capability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: As part of a key measure to prepare for future pandemic, we have to designate medical masks as a critical supply item that requires some local production capability.

sections.label: Reserves drawn for COVID bill
sections.summary: The total bill snowballed to $72.3 billion in FY2020 and FY2021, so the Reserves had to be drawn on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Thereafter, we had to draw on the Reserves as the total bill snowballed to $72.3 billion in FY2020 and FY2021.

sections.label: Business support schemes during COVID
sections.summary: The Jobs Credit Scheme, COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act and various financing support helped businesses stay afloat and safeguarded capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Jobs Credit Scheme, COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act and the various financing support made a big difference to help our business stay afloat and safeguarded our capabilities.

sections.label: Governance and 4G leadership during crisis
sections.summary: The passage agrees with the White Paper's conclusion of high quality governance, and states the 4G team proved its leadership ability during the crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Multi-Ministry Task Force (MTF) also regularly updated Singaporeans on the latest developments in an open and transparent manner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: So, I agree with the White Paper’s conclusion that there has been high quality of governance throughout the crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister and the Cabinet has not only steered the nation into safe harbour during the pandemic but have also set our sights beyond the pandemic with moves and strategies for the country to emerge stronger.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Not that we want it that way, but the crisis came at a time as if to test the leadership strength of the 4G team.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I believe that Deputy Prime Minister Wong and the 4G team has proven their leadership ability, the tenacity, the decisiveness and courage to take difficult decisions in overcoming the crisis, as well as doing what is right and what is in the long-term good for the country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Most importantly, the 4G team has demonstrated that the well-being of Singaporeans is foremost in their minds and hearts.

sections.label: Trust and COVID-19 mortality
sections.summary: Confucius said a nation cannot stand without the people's trust, and an Oxford University study found higher trust linked to lower COVID-19 mortality rates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Confucius said, "Without the people’s trust, a nation cannot stand." A study by Oxford University found that countries with higher levels of trust have lower COVID-19 mortality rates.

sections.label: MTF press conferences during pandemic
sections.summary: During the pandemic's most challenging times, the MTF held press conferences almost daily to inform people and give preventive guidance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: During the most challenging times of the pandemic, the MTF held press conferences almost daily to inform people of the progress of the pandemic control efforts and gave guidance to the people on the preventive measures they should individually take.

sections.label: Mobile vaccination for seniors
sections.summary: When vaccines became available, the Government sent Mobile Vaccination Teams to nursing centres, and vaccination among Singaporean seniors eventually reached 90%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: When vaccines became available, the Government dispatched Mobile Vaccination Teams to nursing centres to vaccinate the elderly and caregivers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Eventually, the vaccination rate among Singaporean seniors reached 90%.

sections.label: Elderly digitalisation transition
sections.summary: About 210,000 elderly people transitioned to digitalisation in the past three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In the past three years, about 210,000 elderly people have transitioned to digitalisation.

sections.label: COVID-19 financial assistance schemes
sections.summary: COVID-19 financial assistance schemes disbursed around $2.3 billion to more than half a million individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Altogether, the COVID-19 financial assistance schemes disbursed around $2.3 billion to more than half a million individuals, helping to ease the financial burden of COVID-19 on those affected most severely.

sections.label: Giving.sg donation platform
sections.summary: Giving.sg raised a record $286 million from 2020 to 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Giving.sg, a one-stop online donation platform, raised a record of $286 million from 2020 to 2022, with many giving more to the social welfare, health and community sectors.

sections.label: Keeping schools open
sections.summary: Schools were kept open most of the time, valuing students' future and parents' lives and livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Furthermore, if children do not go to school for a long time, resulting in a lack of interaction with teachers and classmates, will it affect their social interaction skills and even their physical and mental health?

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Hence, we decided to keep our schools open most of the time, because as much as we value health, we also place great importance on the future of these 604,000 students and 190,000 preschoolers, as well as the lives and livelihoods of all parents.

sections.label: Free mailing for masks
sections.summary: Singapore Post provided free mailing services for masks to needy beneficiaries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Singapore Post provided free mailing services for these masks; by simply writing "Masks Sewn With Love" on the envelope, the masks would be delivered to the needy beneficiaries for free.

sections.label: Singaporeans say country more united
sections.summary: Three out of four Singaporeans said the country was more united than before COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Three out of four Singaporeans said that our country was more united than before COVID-19.

sections.label: White Paper on vulnerable Singaporeans
sections.summary: The White Paper recognised that Singapore did well to support the vulnerable amongst us.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: As the White Paper recognised, Singapore did well to support the vulnerable amongst us.

sections.label: SG United Jobs and Skills Package
sections.summary: Around 200,000 individuals were placed into jobs under the SG United Jobs and Skills Package.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: At the same time, many affected individuals took it upon themselves to utilise various employment support programmes, with around 200,000 individuals placed into jobs under the SG United Jobs and Skills Package.

sections.label: ComLink expansion for rental households
sections.summary: Some 5,000 rental households were promptly given support, and ComLink expanded from four pilot towns to 21 communities nationwide.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Some 5,000 households living in rental housing, who had not previously come forward to seek support and help, were promptly given support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We expanded ComLink from the initial four pilot towns to 21 ComLink communities nationwide, so as to better serve families with children in rental housing.

sections.label: Family Violence Taskforce recommendations
sections.summary: In October 2021 the Government accepted in principle all the Family Violence Taskforce recommendations and is implementing them progressively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In October 2021, the Government accepted in principle all the Family Violence Taskforce recommendations and are implementing them progressively over the next few years.

sections.label: Anxiety and depression during pandemic
sections.summary: Thirteen percent of the general population reported symptoms of anxiety or depression during the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Thirteen percent of the general population reported symptoms of anxiety or depression during the pandemic.

sections.label: Youth mental health and national strategy
sections.summary: About 37% of youths reported a decrease in ability to manage their mental health, and the Inter-agency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-being aims to release a national strategy by year end.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: About 37% of youths in this age group also said there was a decrease in their ability to manage their mental health now compared with before the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
