sentences.text: The Inter-agency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-being that was established during the pandemic is working towards the development of a national strategy for mental health and well-being, and is aiming to release this by the end of the year.

sections.label: Invictus Fund support
sections.summary: The Invictus Fund provided $18 million to support over 300 social service agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In all, the Invictus Fund provided $18 million to support over 300 social service agencies.

sections.label: Refreshing social compact
sections.summary: Forward Singapore refreshes the social compact by tapping individuals, families, communities and public, private and people sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: As we refresh our social compact through Forward Singapore, let us tap on the strengths of individuals and families, the social capital within our communities and the expertise and resources from the public, private and people sectors.

sections.label: Pandemic payouts disbursed
sections.summary: $593 million was disbursed to around 480,000 unique beneficiaries through four pandemic-period grant schemes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: An impressive $593 million was disbursed to around 480,000 unique beneficiaries across the pandemic period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: They were given in the forms of Temporary Relief Fund, COVID-19 Support Grant, COVID-19 Recovery Grant - Temporary and COVID-19 Recovery Grant.

sections.label: Family violence police reports
sections.summary: From 7 April to 6 May 2020, 476 Police reports were filed for family violence offences, a 22% rise over the pre-circuit breaker monthly average.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: From 7 April to 6 May 2020, there were 476 Police reports filed for offences commonly associated with family violence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This was a 22% increase compared with the monthly average of about 389 of such cases before the circuit breaker, according to the Police then.

sections.label: Reasons Singapore weathered storm
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore weathered the storm, citing three reasons: our people, our money, and sheer luck.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: That Singapore had weathered the storm is unmistakable, but the reasons we did so may be less clear.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I count at least three, the third of which is often overlooked: first, our people; second, our money; and third, sheer luck.

sections.label: Migrant worker dormitory outbreak
sections.summary: The passage says opening hearts and doors to migrant workers was right, but not anticipating the dormitory outbreak was a mistake.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I was also proud of the way we opened our hearts and our doors to the migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: It was a mistake not to have anticipated the intensity of the outbreak in the dormitories – it meant that nearly half of the 300,000 workers living in dormitories had been infected by 2020.

sections.label: Community trust during pandemic
sections.summary: The business and Singaporean communities came together and their trust was tested at pivotal pandemic moments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The business community also played their part and the whole Singaporean community also played their part; we all came together, and together, we reaped the returns of the trust, the faith that we had built over the years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Indeed, during the day when DORSCON Orange was declared, when Malaysia announced their Movement Control Order and when we announced our circuit breaker, these were pivotal moments where our trust and our faith and our bonds – these were tested in full force.

sections.label: NTUC Enterprise pandemic support packages
sections.summary: In 2020 NTUC Enterprise social enterprises rolled out a $50-million package, and $20 million more the following year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In 2020, the NTUC Enterprise group of social enterprises rolled out a $50-million package to provide holistic support for Singaporeans to cope with the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In the following year, another $20 million was committed to help the community tide over the second year of the pandemic.

sections.label: FairPrice Supply Chain Ops Centre
sections.summary: By 2021, FairPrice had set up a Supply Chain Ops Centre called SCope.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: By 2021, FairPrice had set up what we called a Supply Chain Ops Centre (SCope).

sections.label: Egg sources during COVID-19
sections.summary: Eggs come from Malaysia, Australia, New Zealand and local farms, with Spain, Ukraine and Poland added during COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: So, yes, whilst we still carry a lot of eggs from Malaysia, we also have eggs from Australia, New Zealand as well as, certainly, from our local farms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: And over this COVID-19 period, we have added Spain, Ukraine and Poland as additional sources for eggs.

sections.label: Stockpiling review and fore-planning team
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the revised critical items list is made public and welcomes a fore-planning team for future crises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In reviewing our stockpiling strategies, I hope the Government will make the revised comprehensive list of critical items known to the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong mentioned, I was glad to hear that there will be a fore-planning team and department that will be set up for future crises.

sections.label: Safe distancing and aviation redeployment
sections.summary: About 3,000 Safe Distancing Ambassadors were deployed by MSE, and PSD redeployed aviation workers when flights were suspended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: One example would be how around 3,000 Safe Distancing Ambassadors and enforcement officers were deployed and coordinated by the Ministry of Sustainability and Environment (MSE) to ensure compliance with safe management measures (SMMs) and vaccination-differentiated SMMs in public spaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: When commercial flights were suspended during the height of the pandemic, the Public Service Division (PSD) quickly worked with the private sector to redeploy aviation workers to fill urgent manpower needs in both public healthcare institutions and public agencies.

sections.label: Foreign workers and manpower vulnerabilities
sections.summary: The speaker hopes MOM and agencies are reviewing foreign worker and pass holder data to assess and mitigate manpower vulnerabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While it should remain Singapore's strength to remain open to the world even in trying times, the prolonged pandemic has seen expatriates and migrant workers return home to be with their families with no certainty of return.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I hope MOM and relevant agencies are already looking or will be looking at the data on the trend of foreign workers and pass holders from before the pandemic up till today, to assess and mitigate our manpower vulnerabilities going forward.

sections.label: Digital devices and online religious content
sections.summary: MENDAKI helped students get digital devices, while Muis, mosques and Islamic education providers helped asatizah provide religious content online.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: MENDAKI also helped our students in need to procure digital devices for online learning, while Muis, the mosques and Islamic education centres and providers helped equip our asatizah with the skills to provide religious content online.

sections.label: GovTech solutions and digital comfort
sections.summary: GovTech rolled out SafeEntry and TraceTogether, and ordinary Singaporeans became comfortable operating in the digital space.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Not only has GovTech rolled out nationwide, data-driven tech solutions like SafeEntry and TraceTogether as part of our pandemic management measures, ordinary Singaporeans have also gotten comfortable with operating in the digital space.

sections.label: NEA and SFA hawker outreach
sections.summary: NEA and SFA outreach to stallholders helped achieve 99.9% vaccination and rostered routine testing, letting hawker centres, wet markets and coffee shops maintain operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This is all, in part, down to the efforts of NEA and SFA to reach out to stallholders during the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: These intensive outreach efforts had also helped to achieve a 99.9% vaccination rate across hawker centres, wet markets and coffee shops and to implement the rostered routine testing regime to test thousands of hawkers and workers, which allowed our hawker centres, wet markets and coffee shops, to maintain operations and serve the local communities.

sections.label: Pandemic partnerships and frontline workers
sections.summary: The speaker credits close partnership and trust among stakeholders, Singaporeans and frontline workers for progress, and urges repeating key White Paper points.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: As I looked back, I cannot help but remember my interactions and engagements with residents as they reached out for assistance during the pandemic, which I think I should share some of it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Much has happened over the last three years and what has made it possible for us to be where we are today are the close partnership and trust amongst all stakeholders – Government, agencies, businesses, private and people sectors and, most importantly, Singaporeans and those living in Singapore and interacting with Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: We must thank our frontline workers and everyone who contributed, many who worked hard behind the scenes, unknown and unseen, and probably will never be known by many of us, and the many sacrifices that were made in this journey.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: While we debate today on what went right or wrong, let us not miss some key points made in the White Paper which I think are worth repeating.

sections.label: Trusted nodes and communication SOPs
sections.summary: The speaker proposes trusted frontline crisis communication nodes, SOPs for resident communication channels, and SOPs for two-way engagement with agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: As the Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong had said in his speech, "realistically we can plan or invest but we cannot plan for every situation." I am proposing that one, we identify, designate and setup in "peacetime" trusted nodes of frontline crisis communication by areas or by constituencies, closer to the community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Two, establish standard operating procedures (SOP) of communication with residents and channels of engagement and points of contacts, for example, the number to call, email addresses and WhatApp.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Three, establish SOPs for two-way communication and appropriate engagement between the nodes and agencies including the latest information updates and escalation handling.

sections.label: Frontline crisis communication network
sections.summary: Proposes a regularly exercised community frontline and crisis communication network for activation during pandemics or national crises.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: While my recommendations are not novel and parts of this already exists, what I am proposing is a deliberate move to forward plan, as Deputy Prime Minister Wong has said earlier, and put in place a network and system for frontline communications and crisis communication closer to the community that is regularly exercised and tested, so that we can activate them during a pandemic or any other national crisis.

sections.label: Science, technology and essential goods
sections.summary: White Paper highlights boosting science and technology for pandemic detection and response, maintaining committees, drills, and production of masks, test kits and vaccines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As the White Paper has highlighted, Singapore needs to continue to boost its science and technology capabilities to deal with future pandemic detection, management and response.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We must continue to have the strategic committee and task force to carry out regular exercises and drills as the next pandemic could be much worse and fatal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We need to maintain our production capability and capacity for essential goods, such as masks and test kits as well as vaccines.

sections.label: Improving HDB housing designs
sections.summary: Asks whether the Housing and Development Board can look into improving housing designs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Can the Housing and Development Board (HDB) look into how we can improve on our housing designs?

sections.label: Testing capacity of 60,000 tests
sections.summary: Singapore built up a testing capacity of up to 60,000 tests a day despite challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Despite all the challenges, Singapore was able to build up a testing capacity of up to 60,000 tests a day.

sections.label: Safe Distancing Ambassadors and Enforcement Officers
sections.summary: Over 3,000 Safe Distancing Ambassadors and Enforcement Officers were deployed daily at public areas; Jurong Spring had zero COVID-19 deaths in markets and hawker centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: At the height of the pandemic, over 3,000 Safe Distancing Ambassadors and Enforcement Officers were deployed daily at public areas such as malls, parks, hawker centres, and coffee shops to ensure compliance with SMMs and VDS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In addition, there are over 114 hawker centres and wet markets and over 1,200 coffee shops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Overall, in Jurong Spring, there was zero COVID-19 deaths within the market and hawker centres, and all the hawker centres and market stalls remain open till today.

sections.label: NEA, SFA outreach and testing
sections.summary: NEA and SFA outreach achieved 99.9% stallholder vaccination, and with HPB ran Rostered Routine Testing for about 24,000 hawkers and 39,000 food court workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: The officers were understanding, pragmatic and agile in their execution to ensure that operations were conducted safely, but yet nuanced with commercial and economic practicalities when possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: This strong working relationship was further validated when collectively together with the local community, NEA and SFA conducted intensive outreach efforts and achieved a 99.9% vaccination rate among stallholders rapidly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Between July 2021 and February 2022, NEA and SFA also worked with the Health Promotion Board (HPB) to implement the Rostered Routine Testing (RRT) regime, which regularly tested around 24,000 hawkers and stakeholders at markets and hawker centres, as well as some 39,000 workers in food courts and coffee shops.

sections.label: Heartland shops and hawkers digital
sections.summary: This addresses enabling heartland shops to operate remotely during the pandemic, recalling the Hawkers Go Digital programme launched by MCI in June 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: This was in response to the need to enable heartland shops to operate remotely and maintain their businesses during the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: I remembered how useful it was to the hawkers when MCI launched the Hawkers Go Digital programme in June 2020.

sections.label: Digital Ambassadors Programme for seniors
sections.summary: MCI increased digital adoption among seniors and vulnerable groups during the pandemic by launching the Digital Ambassadors Programme, which recruited and trained volunteers to help seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, yet again, MCI worked hard to increase digital adoption among seniors and vulnerable groups during the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: It launched the Digital Ambassadors Programme, which recruited and trained volunteers to help seniors.

sections.label: Pandemic deaths and Singapore recession
sections.summary: Over 6.6 million lives were lost globally including 1,331 in Singapore, and the economy contracted by 4.4%, its worst recession since Independence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Over 6.6 million lives were lost globally, including 1,331 in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Our country's economy contracted by 4.4% and suffered its worst recession since Independence.

sections.label: Passenger traffic pandemic low
sections.summary: At the height of the pandemic, passenger traffic fell to its lowest levels ever, barely reaching 0.5% of 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: At the height of the pandemic, passenger traffic fell to its lowest levels ever, barely reaching 0.5% of 2019.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme saved jobs
sections.summary: The Jobs Support Scheme helped businesses affected by the economic slowdown by paying workers' salaries, saving an estimated 165,000 jobs and reducing the unemployment rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Jobs Support Scheme (JSS), for example, helped businesses affected by the economic slowdown by paying for their workers' salaries, saving an estimated 165,000 jobs and reducing the unemployment rate.

sections.label: Industries pivoted during pandemic
sections.summary: Industries pivoted during the pandemic, such as aerospace where airlines converted aircraft to carry more cargo and airline workers moved to vaccination centres or other industries while upskilling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: At times, we had to pivot to meet and overcome these new challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This was exemplified by various industries during the pandemic such as the aerospace industry, where airlines converted their aircraft to carry more cargo and airline workers moved to man vaccination centres or across different industries while upskilling and retraining themselves.

sections.label: SGBukaPuasa food rations
sections.summary: The SGBukaPuasa initiative distributed over 300,000 food rations to needy residents during Ramadan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For example, the SGBukaPuasa initiative has distributed more than 300,000 food rations to needy residents throughout the month of Ramadan.

sections.label: Seven COVID-19 lessons
sections.summary: The paper highlights seven key lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The paper highlights seven key lessons that we can learn from our experience through the COVID-19 pandemic.

sections.label: Unity and next pandemic
sections.summary: Infrastructure, supply chain and policy efforts will be futile without societal unity, and the next pandemic is a question of when.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While it is essential to work on infrastructure, supply chain and policies to make us more resilient, these efforts will be futile if we do not stay united as a society and exhibit the values that have made us stronger during this challenging period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is critical to recognise that the next pandemic is not a question of "if" but "when" it will happen and Disease X may be even more dangerous than COVID-19.

sections.label: Societal values for next pandemic

sections.summary: Air hub passenger traffic fell to less than 0.5% of pre-COVID-19 traffic, and about one-third of staff lost jobs or were redeployed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: At one point, our air hub's passenger traffic fell to less than 0.5% of pre-COVID-19 traffic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: About one-third of the staff lost their jobs or got redeployed to other sectors.

sections.label: Passenger numbers rebound
sections.summary: Over the last 10 months, passenger numbers rebounded from 2% to 80%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Over the last 10 months, passenger numbers rebounded from 2% to 80%.

sections.label: Estimated COVID-19 deaths
sections.summary: MOH estimated an additional 2,000 deaths over the pandemic, with over 3,700 deaths in all, mostly older people with co-morbidities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: MOH estimated an additional 2,000 deaths over the course of the pandemic – that is above the expected number of deaths based on pre-pandemic trends.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: All in, over 3,700 deaths, estimated – most of them older, with co-morbidities, underlying illnesses, many unvaccinated and they are most affected by COVID-19 infections.

sections.label: Vaccines lowered severe disease
sections.summary: MOH data shows that during the 2022 Omicron waves, vaccines lowered the probability of severe disease and deaths for the elderly by more than five times.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Our latest MOH data shows that during the Omicron waves of 2022, vaccines lowered the probability of severe disease and deaths for the elderly by more than five times.

sections.label: Vaccine coverage and Workers' Party support
sections.summary: Most Singaporeans trusted the recommendations, over 90% vaccine coverage was achieved, and the Workers' Party is thanked for supporting the vaccination effort.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Fortunately, the great majority of Singaporeans and the public trusted our recommendations to take the vaccines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We achieved over 90% vaccine coverage and I thank the Workers' Party for supporting this very pivotal national effort to vaccinate our population.

sections.label: Public hospital bed occupancy
sections.summary: Public hospital bed occupancy rose from a pre-COVID level of 87.6% in 2019 to 93.1% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Our public hospital bed occupancy has risen, from a pre-COVID level of 87.6% in 2019, to 93.1% in 2022.

sections.label: Average length of stay
sections.summary: The average rose from 6.1 days in 2019 to seven days in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: From an average of 6.1 days in 2019, to seven days in 2022.

sections.label: Pandemic TCF beds setup
sections.summary: During the pandemic, 500 TCF beds were set up across five sites run by five private healthcare providers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: During the pandemic, we set up 500 TCF beds across five sites operated by five private sector healthcare providers.

sections.label: TCFs as long-term feature
sections.summary: TCFs will become a medium or long-term feature, retaining current facilities including Changi Expo Hall 9 primarily as a TCF.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We have, therefore, decided that TCFs will become a medium or even long-term feature of our healthcare system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We will retain the current facilities, including continuing to use Changi Expo Hall 9 primarily as a TCF.

sections.label: PREPARE epidemic research programme
sections.summary: PREPARE, launched in November last year, is the national epidemic R&D plan and a major initiative from the crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As Dr Tan Wu Meng and Mr Yip Hon Weng have pointed out, we need strong public health scientific and research capabilities to quickly assess these key characteristics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It stands for the Programme for Research in Epidemic Preparedness and Response that I launched in November last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This is our national epidemic R&D plan and a major initiative arising from the crisis.

sections.label: GISAID genomic data platform
sections.summary: GISAID, a global non-profit platform for open sharing of pathogen genomic data, will work closely with Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: GISAID played an instrumental role during the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It is a global non-profit platform for open sharing of genomic data of viral pathogens and, today, it is the world’s largest repository of SARS-CoV-2 sequences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Singapore will work closely with GISAID, and they have established a base here in collaboration with A*STAR.

sections.label: New Communicable Diseases Agency
sections.summary: A new CDA under MOH will oversee preparedness, prevention, control, surveillance, risk assessment and outbreak response, consolidating public health functions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: To do so, we will set up a new Communicable Diseases Agency, or CDA, under MOH.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It will oversee disease preparedness, prevention and control, surveillance, risk assessment and outbreak response.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This new agency will consolidate the relevant public health functions that, today, reside in MOH, National Centre for Infectious Diseases (NCID) as well as the Health Promotion Board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The National Public Health Laboratory (NPHL) is a critical national resource and will be transferred to the CDA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The CDA will maintain oversight of the clinical facilities in NCID.

sections.label: Permanent Crisis Strategy Group
sections.summary: MOH will separately retain a permanent Crisis Strategy and Operations Group in the Ministry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In addition, MOH will separately retain a permanent Crisis Strategy and Operations Group, or CSOG, in the Ministry.

sections.label: Healthcare Reserve Force setup
sections.summary: A Healthcare Reserve Force will be set up, made up of ex-healthcare workers and volunteers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In addition, we will set up a Healthcare Reserve Force, made up of ex-healthcare workers and volunteers.

sections.label: IDA two public health worlds
sections.summary: IDA currently envisages only two worlds of public health: peacetime or public health emergency, with no gradations in between.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As it stands now, IDA envisages only two worlds of public health: peacetime or public health emergency, with no gradations in between.

sections.label: Rescinding CTMA Part 7
sections.summary: If amendments pass, Part 7 of CTMA can be rescinded, and four public health situational tiers are envisaged under amended IDA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Once the amendments are tabled and if passed by the House, we can and we intend to rescind Part 7 of CTMA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Just to share some preliminary thinking, we envisage four public health situational tiers under the amended IDA.

sections.label: Four tiers replacing DORSCON
sections.summary: The four situational tiers can replace DORSCON colour coding, and the law spells out measures for each situational state.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: When these changes come into effect, we can also use these four situational tiers to replace the current DORSCON colour coding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I think it is more intuitive to tell the public that there is an outbreak, a threat, or an emergency, as opposed to colours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And the law spells out what measures could take place under each situational state.

sections.label: Singapore vaccine procurement workgroup
sections.summary: Singapore was first in Asia to obtain enough COVID-19 vaccines, and an inter-agency workgroup developed the vaccine procurement approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Despite our small size and despite the worldwide shortage, Singapore was the first country in Asia to obtain COVID-19 vaccines, enough for all our people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: During the early phase of the pandemic, we set up an inter-agency workgroup chaired by the Head of Civil Service and comprising senior officials from agencies, such as Prime Minister's Office (PMO), MOH, the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR), Economy Development Board (EDB) and Health Sciences Authority (HSA), to develop our vaccine procurement approach.

sections.label: Portfolio approach recommendation
sections.summary: On what to buy, the workgroup recommended a portfolio approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: On the first question of what to buy, the workgroup recommended a portfolio approach.

sections.label: Advance purchase vaccine agreements
sections.summary: Singapore used relationships with pharmaceutical companies to make advance purchase agreements with fixed delivery schedules and quantities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: On the question of how to secure assured and early delivery, we leveraged our relationships with the pharmaceutical companies and entered into advance purchase agreements with fixed delivery schedules and quantities.

sections.label: Expired vaccine doses cost
sections.summary: Expired vaccines are about 15% of ordered doses, worth S$140 million, and may rise to close to 25%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: To date, expired vaccines are about 15% of the doses we ordered, with a total value of S$140 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In the coming months, this is likely to rise to close to 25%, as more vaccines expire.

sections.label: Circuit breaker GDP loss
sections.summary: The two-month circuit breaker cost around $11 billion in gross domestic product loss.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The two-month circuit breaker cost us around $11 billion in terms of gross domestic product (GDP) loss.

sections.label: Six vaccine manufacturing plants
sections.summary: Through EDB's efforts, Singapore will anchor six vaccine manufacturing plants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Fifth, through the Economic Development Board's (EDB's) efforts, we will be anchoring six vaccine manufacturing plants in Singapore.

sections.label: Dr Tan Chee Keat isolation chamber
sections.summary: Dr Tan Chee Keat at Ng Teng Fong Hospital was part of the team developing a negative pressure isolation chamber for intubating infectious COVID-19 patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Dr Tan Chee Keat at Ng Teng Fong Hospital, who was part of the team to develop a negative pressure isolation chamber used to intubate infectious COVID-19 patients and helped keep her team safe during dangerous procedures.

sections.label: Nurse Solacito COVID-19 care
sections.summary: Ms Christine Joy Cordevilla Solacito used MERS and Ebola experience to care for early COVID-19-positive patients from Wuhan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Ms Christine Joy Cordevilla Solacito, Senior Staff Nurse at Singapore General Hospital, who used her experience with MERS and Ebola to handle early COVID-19-positive patients from Wuhan, when she cared for ICU patients, administered chemotherapy in the isolation ward and delivered babies for the COVID-19-positive pregnant mothers.

sections.label: Driver-medic pair pandemic work
sections.summary: A driver-medic pair from Ambulance Medical Services worked 14-hour days for weeks, making up to 16 trips a day ferrying COVID-19 patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Mr Mahmod bin Mohd Yahya and Mr Humam Sufi bin Mohamed Ali, they are a driver-medic pair from Ambulance Medical Services Pte Ltd, who at the height of the pandemic, they worked 14-hour days for several weeks, making up to 16 trips a day to ferry patients to and from COVID-19 care facilities.

sections.label: Writing Singapore's next chapter
sections.summary: The passage states that writing the next chapter will bring better hospitals, more complete laws and more secure vaccines and medical supplies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: If we do, then, in the next chapter, our hospitals and healthcare systems will be better, our laws more complete, our vaccines and medical supplies more secure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, we write our next chapter, not knowing whether the world will dawn bright or dark, be hostile or friendly; but confident in ourselves that Singapore has become stronger through this crisis and we can stand taller to meet the next one.

sections.label: Singapore 2020 recession contraction
sections.summary: The world economy halted in 2020 and Singapore's economy contracted by 3.9%, its worst recession since Independence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Indeed, the world economy ground to a halt in 2020 and the Singapore economy contracted by 3.9% – our worst recession since Independence.

sections.label: Daily mask utilisation rate
sections.summary: Singapore was looking at a utilisation rate of more than five million masks each day, about one month's public healthcare need.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: In Singapore's case, we were looking at a utilisation rate of more than five million masks each day, around the number required by the public healthcare system for one month.

sections.label: StayMasked vending machines and food imports
sections.summary: Temasek Foundation's StayMasked vending machines distributed over 31 million reusable masks by end-2021, and Singapore imports over 90% of its food.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Many of you would be familiar with the Temasek Foundation's StayMasked vending machines installed across the island.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: They distributed a total of more than 31 million reusable masks to Singapore residents by the end of 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: As we know, Singapore imports more than 90% of our food from overseas.

sections.label: New food import arrangements
sections.summary: Singapore secured new import arrangements for eggs, vegetables, chicken, shrimps, dried fruits and tomatoes, and set up the SNAP air bridge.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: During the pandemic, we secured new import arrangements for eggs, frozen vegetables and frozen chicken from Poland, red sea shrimps from Saudi Arabia, dried fruits from Uzbekistan and tomatoes from Türkiye.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We also established the Singapore-New Zealand Airfreight Project, or SNAP in short, in April 2020 to provide a secure, two-way "air bridge" to carry almost 140 metric tons of food supplies to Singapore and medical supplies back to New Zealand.

sections.label: Supply chain resilience strategies
sections.summary: The Government used import diversification, local manufacturing capability and stockpiling to enhance supply chain resilience.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The Government has employed a combination of strategies to enhance our supply chain resilience: first, diversification of imports; second, enhancing our local manufacturing capability; and finally, stockpiling.

sections.label: Border closure timing
sections.summary: With hindsight, border measures could have been tightened earlier when signs of virus spreading across borders appeared.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Border closures are also highly disruptive to businesses, travellers and families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Now, with the benefit of hindsight, we could have erred on the side of caution and tightened border measures earlier when there were signs of virus spreading across borders, even if there had not been any large infection clusters here.

sections.label: Vaccinated Travel Lanes pilot
sections.summary: When over 75% of the Singapore population was fully vaccinated, the Vaccinated Travel Lanes were piloted in September 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: When more than 75% of the Singapore population was fully vaccinated, we decided to pilot the Vaccinated Travel Lanes in September 2021.

sections.label: Aviation recovery and infrastructure
sections.summary: Changi Airport passenger traffic is expected to recover to pre-COVID-19 levels by 2024, and the Government provided close to $2.5 billion of aviation support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Passenger traffic through Changi Airport is expected to recover to pre-COVID-19 levels by 2024 and we are also making good progress on our long-term infrastructure projects, such as Changi Terminal 5 and Tuas Port.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Since the start of the pandemic, the Government has provided close to $2.5 billion of support towards the aviation sector's recovery.

sections.label: COVID-19 Budgets business support
sections.summary: Through eight COVID-19 Budgets, the Government provided more than $72 billion of support for businesses and workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Through the eight COVID-19 Budgets, the Government provided more than $72 billion of support for businesses and workers and these include: (a) Enhancements to the Enterprise Financing Scheme and the introduction of the Temporary Bridging Loan Scheme, which helped small and medium enterprises address their cashflow difficulties; (b) Enhancements to capability development grants, like the Enterprise Development Grant, Market Readiness Assistance and Productivity Solutions Grant, which helped businesses transform and enhance their competitive edge in preparation for recovery; (c) Wage support for employers to help them retain their local workers during the COVID-19 pandemic, such as the Job Support Scheme; and (d) Support measures for businesses affected by the SMMs, such as the Rental Support Scheme and Small Business Recovery Grant.

sections.label: Formula 1 night race return
sections.summary: The Formula 1 night race was brought back in 2022, attracting more than 300,000 participants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Notably, we also brought back the Formula 1 night race in 2022, which attracted more than 300,000 participants.

sections.label: SRV scheme hotel beneficiaries
sections.summary: More than 450 hotels, attractions and tour providers benefited from the SRV scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: More than 450 hotels, attractions and tour providers benefited from this SRV scheme.

sections.label: Heartland enterprises e-payment adoption
sections.summary: Around 93% of heartland enterprises have adopted e-payment solutions, almost 40% more than before the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To date, I am happy to say that around 93% of our heartland enterprises have adopted e-payment solutions, which is almost 40% more than before the pandemic.

sections.label: National Awards COVID-19 recipients
sections.summary: About 10,000 individuals and teams from various sectors will receive the National Awards (COVID-19) for their contributions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: A total of about 10,000 individuals and teams from the people, public, healthcare and private sectors will receive the National Awards (COVID-19), in recognition of their contributions to our COVID-19 efforts.

sections.label: Companies setting up Singapore Expo beds
sections.summary: Companies worked as a team to set up the first 960 beds at Singapore Expo, later expanded to around 8,000 beds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Companies, like PSA International, Surbana Jurong, SingEx, Certis Cisco, ST Engineering, Parkway Pantai, Sheares Healthcare, Woodlands Health Campus and Resorts World Sentosa (RWS), worked as a team to set up the first 960 beds within record time at the Singapore Expo, which eventually expanded to around 8,000 beds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: RWS involved all its business units to also set-up and run other CCFs and recruited over 2,000 volunteers to ensure smooth operations.

sections.label: Hotels and retail leasing code
sections.summary: Singapore Hotel Association and Singapore Tourism Board worked with over 90 hotels to transform them into isolation facilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For example, the Singapore Hotel Association and the Singapore Tourism Board worked closely with over 90 hotels across the island, to urgently transform hotels into Government isolation facilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The Singapore Business Federation worked together with Enterprise Singapore, other TACs, landlords and tenant representatives, on a Code of Conduct for Leasing of Retail Premises.

sections.label: Three themes from Members' points
sections.summary: Members' points can be summarised into three themes: preparing for the next pandemic, ensuring spending effectiveness, and upholding solidarity and trust.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The points raised by Members can be summarised into three broad themes: first, preparing for the next pandemic; second, ensuring effectiveness of our spending; and third, upholding solidarity and trust.

sections.label: Consolidated COVID-19 White Paper
sections.summary: The Prime Minister's Office was tasked to produce a consolidated report, released as a White Paper, after the situation stabilised.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Because the situation had stabilised, and we could envisage a full transition to endemic COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: There was therefore a need to pull together the findings from Mr Peter Ho's interim report and the agency AARs, as well as the lessons from our more recent experiences, into a consolidated report that would fully reflect all that had transpired over the last three years and provide a fuller synthesis of all our learnings.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And that is why PMO – the Prime Minister's Office – was tasked to put together this consolidated report, which the Government decided to release as a White Paper.

sections.label: White Paper scope
sections.summary: The White Paper is more comprehensive than Mr Ho's review, including agencies' AARs and learnings after August 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The White Paper is, in fact, more comprehensive than what Mr Ho's review has set out to cover, because it includes information from the agencies' AARs as well as learnings from our experience after August 2021.

sections.label: Economic resilience measures
sections.summary: Economic resilience requires investing in local production, diversifying import sources, and strengthening infrastructure and transport links.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In economic resilience, as Mr Shawn Huang, Mr Seah Kian Peng, Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Saktiandi Supaat said, we need to invest in alternatives like local production, diversify our import sources and strengthen the robustness of our infrastructure and transport links.

sections.label: WHO outbreak alerts 2021
sections.summary: In summer 2021 the WHO received alerts on over 5,000 new outbreaks, most not making global headlines as spillovers fade quickly.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Just in the summer of 2021 alone, when we were all focusing on and grappling with COVID-19, the World Health Organization (WHO) received alerts on more than 5,000 new outbreaks around the world, few of which made global headlines, because most spillovers lead to smaller clusters of disease that quickly die out.

sections.label: COVAX and Pandemic Fund
sections.summary: Singapore co-chaired the Friends of COVAX Facility, and the G20 set up a Global Health Security Financial Intermediary Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Singapore was a co-chair of the Friends of the COVID-19 Vaccine Global Access (COVAX) Facility, which helped countries in need secure access to COVID-19 vaccines.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The G20 recently set up a Global Health Security Financial Intermediary Fund, or what is now called The Pandemic Fund, to ensure more reliable financing for future pandemics.

sections.label: COVID-19 mortality rate
sections.summary: As of 31 December 2022, Singapore's COVID-19 mortality rate was around 300 deaths per million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In terms of lives, as of 31 December 2022, our mortality rate for COVID-19 was around 300 deaths per million.

sections.label: COVID-19 budget spending total
sections.summary: More than $100 billion was budgeted and $72.3 billion spent over FY2020 and FY2021, about 15% of FY2020 GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As I mentioned yesterday, we had budgeted more than $100 billion and we eventually spent $72.3 billion over FY2020 and FY2021, which is equivalent to about 15% of our FY2020 GDP.

sections.label: Avoiding school closure scarring
sections.summary: Other places had lengthy school closures with long-term scarring effects, while Singapore kept businesses afloat and unemployment low through JSS and other financing support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This was not the case in many other places, where lengthy school closures had long-term scarring effects, in terms of human capital development, particularly for students from less advantaged backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We kept businesses afloat and local unemployment rates low through the JSS and other financing support.

sections.label: Government spending to beneficiaries
sections.summary: More than 80% of Government spending went directly to beneficiaries to keep businesses going, preserve jobs and help those hard-hit by the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: More than 80% of the Government spending went directly to beneficiaries, as I have mentioned, to keep businesses going, preserve jobs for Singaporeans and help those who were hard-hit by the pandemic, especially the vulnerable.

sections.label: Jobs saved by JSS
sections.summary: Estimates show 165,000 jobs were saved in 2020 as a result of JSS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Our estimates show that 165,000 jobs were saved in 2020, as a result of JSS.

sections.label: Breakdown of Government spending
sections.summary: More than 80% of Government spending went to beneficiaries, 10% to grants for medical providers and 10% to procurement with third-parties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As I had explained earlier, more than 80% of Government's spending went directly to beneficiaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Another 10% was for grants to medical providers and the remaining 10% was procurement with third-parties.

sections.label: Temasek community funds for COVID-19
sections.summary: Over three years Temasek redirected a significant proportion of community funds to fight COVID-19, decided independently of the Government, with no draw on Past Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Over the last three years, because we were fighting a crisis, Temasek redirected a significant proportion of these community funds to support the fight against COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This is a decision that Temasek and its Board made, independently of the Government, and there is no draw on Past Reserves from such spending.

sections.label: Post-COVID-19 social capital survey
sections.summary: A Ministry of Communications and Information survey found social capital grew during the pandemic, with over seven in 10 residents saying neighbour and friend relationships stayed the same or strengthened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: A post-COVID-19 survey commissioned by the Ministry of Communications and Information, showed that social capital grew over the course of the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: More than seven in 10 Singapore residents felt that their relationships with their neighbours and friends remained the same or became stronger during the pandemic.

sections.label: Border measures and SMM parameters
sections.summary: Border measures now include Not-to-Land, pre-departure or on-arrival tests, quarantine at home or dedicated facilities, and electronic tagging, while five key SMM parameters are identified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For example, look at border measures, we now have a wider range of measures to apply at the borders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We can impose Not-to-Land (NTL), which is the most stringent; we can allow travellers to enter Singapore, subject to tests and the test can be pre-departure tests or on-arrival tests; we can allow them to come in, subject to both tests and quarantine requirements, and the quarantine can be done at home or in dedicated facilities; and if it is done at home, we have improved the system now so that we have electronic tagging and remote monitoring, it is quite effective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For SMMs, we have identified the five key parameters which are important: group sizes, mask wearing, workplace requirements, safe distancing and capacity limits.

sections.label: External security threat structures
sections.summary: The same structures are used for external security threats, so part of the report cannot be published for national security reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The same structures are used for dealing with external security threats and that is why we are unable to publish that part of the report for national security reasons.

sections.label: Redacting sensitive materials
sections.summary: Redacting all sensitive materials would leave essentially the lessons for the Government, which are already in the White Paper.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: If we redact all of these sensitive materials, we will essentially end up with the lessons for the Government, which are already in the White Paper.

sections.label: Minister Ong on reopening threshold
sections.summary: Minister Ong had replied that defining a definitive full reopening threshold and devising an index would not be wise or useful, but announced four public health situational tiers under an amended Infectious Diseases Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Minister Ong replied then, that it would not be wise to define a definitive threshold for full reopening and that it would not be very useful to devise an index to guide our public health actions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
